Measured against reference/shots/ui-bar.png, our art (hero band, excluding the centre text column) has p99 luma 83.2 and only 0.66% of pixels above luma 100; the reference is p99 195.7 with 9.20% above 100 — 14x more lit pixels. The character region scores 1.43 mean adjacent-pixel luma delta vs the reference's 6.67 (4.7x less surface detail) and tops out at luma 113, i.e. there is not one specular highlight on it. Target, and verify with the same script: art p99 luma >= 180, >7% of pixels above luma 100, character-region detail delta >= 5.0, and the figure enlarged to fill roughly the right 40% of the band with readable armour/cloth planes and a hard rim light at 230+. Everything else on this screen is already close; this one asset is what loses the A/B.
evidence:
HOW INSPECTED: npm run dev (server already up on 5174); npm run shot -- http://localhost:5174/ progress/shots/home-hero-r1-critic.png -> real 780x1688 @DPR2 PNG. Opened it beside reference/shots/ui-bar.png (1008x1792). Built crops at progress/shots/home-hero-r1-critic-ab.png. All colour claims below are sampled pixels via PIL, not eyeballed. npm run verify = 20/20 including no-raw-hex.

BLIND A/B: not close. Cropped both hero bands, stripped nothing else, asked which is the shipped product. The right one, instantly. Ours reads as a dark placeholder: a faceless smooth-shaded mannequin in a cloak (no face, no hands, no armour plates, a stick for a weapon), a flat gold-brown blocky castle silhouette, a smooth featureless tube-arch sweeping across the top-right and muddying the area behind the currency chips, and a flat purple sky. The reference has five depth planes with aerial perspective, a moonlit sky, an embroidered tattered cape, and fully rendered plate with a violet visor glow. Numbers back the eye: character region unique-colour density 3.44% vs 6.43%, adjacent-pixel luma delta 1.43 vs 6.67, max luma 113 vs 255. The raw asset itself is the problem, not the scrim: ember-gate.png alone is mean 27.4 / p99 110.3 / 1.32% above 100.

WHAT HOLDS (credit where due): Trap 1 is clean — every secondary label computes to rgb(196,200,202)=#C4C8CA at opacity 1, no fading anywhere; hierarchy is carried by size + letter-spacing (11px/1.1px labels, 57.2px numeral). Layout rhythm, panel radii, 12/16/20 gaps and the chamfered CLAIM plate are near 1:1 with the bar. Zero scroll confirmed: documentElement scrollHeight 844 == clientHeight 844, scrollWidth 390 == clientWidth 390. Strings are clean — rendered innerText grepped for the RuneScape metal ladder / skill / item names and for FFVI proper nouns: zero hits in shipped copy (the only 'rune' matches are an SVG path id and a comment).

MEASURED FAILURES BEYOND THE ART:
1. Trap 3 (empty track == panel) is broken, and the sign is inverted vs the reference. At the main bar row y=818: our empty track is #13181C (L23.0) while the panel immediately beside it at the same row is #181C20 (L27.3) — the track is 4.3 DARKER, i.e. a well. In the reference at its bar row y=904 the track fill is L~23.0 against a panel of L~19.0 — 3-4 LIGHTER. Root cause: .panel uses --grad-panel, a vertical gradient (#13171B at top, measured drifting to #1B1F24 by y=899), while --c-track is pinned to the panel's TOP value, so it only matches at the very top of a panel and goes dark everywhere else.
2. The track rim is half-strength and has no bevel. Reference cross-section through the empty track: top edge L62.2/58.2 (#3C3F40), bottom edge L52.7 — a lit top lip and a shaded bottom, a real well. Ours: top L32.3 and bottom L32.3 (#1D2125) — symmetric and dim. tokens.css ALREADY defines --c-track-rim #3C4042 (L63.3) and --c-track-rim-lo #33373A (L52.8), correctly measured, but .bar in primitives.css uses 'box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--c-hairline)' (rgba white .045) instead. Those two tokens are wired only in skill.css, so the flagship screen shipped the worse version of the shared primitive it supposedly owns.
3. Divider contrast is ~2.3x too weak. Ours at y=852: #1D2227 (L33.1) on a panel of L28.3 = 1.17x. Reference at y=948: #313431 (L50.8) on a panel of L18.0 = 2.7x, continuous across the full panel width (verified at x=80..900). Cause is the same class of bug: .divider uses --c-groove-cut, which primitives.css defines as color-mix(--c-groove 52%, --c-ground), halving the correctly-measured --c-groove #33383D. skill.css overrides --c-groove-cut back to full --c-groove; home does not. NOTE FOR THE RECORD: reference/ui-bar.md's 'correction 2' (dividers darker than the panel) is contradicted by the actual PNG — the divider is measurably brighter. tokens.css already documents this; the builder was right to follow the pixels. The defect is the magnitude, not the direction.
4. Icons are flat glyphs, not rendered objects. The bar's marks are little modelled things — a coin with a rim, a faceted gem, a steel helm, a gold chevron with shading, a violet portal ring. Ours are single-fill silhouettes with one bevel pass: the coin is a cog, the nav 'ADEPT' helm reads as a capsule with a slot, 'SKILLS' reads as a stack of plates, 'WARDENS' as an almond. Palette slip too: our WARDEN SEALS crown renders white where the reference's crown is gold — a neutral used where an accent belongs.
5. Type floor is below the reference's stated scale. The doc puts small labels at ~11-13px; 'AETHER SHARD' and 'WARDEN SEALS' compute to 8px and the nav labels to 9px. Some of the hierarchy is being bought by shrinking rather than by the scale.
6. Composition dead space: the bottom third of our hero band is near-black with 'IDLE YIELD READY' floating in a void (band mean luma 27.8 vs the reference's 45.1), because the scrim crushes art that had no light in it to begin with. The reference keeps readable art right down to the panel edge.
7. hero.css:141 uses a drop-shadow filter on the crest, against the doc's explicit 'no drop shadows, no gratuitous glow'. Minor, but it is the one place the rule is broken on this screen.

VERDICT: the cabinet is genuinely good — an 85 on its own. The painting inside it is a 35, and the painting is the top 40% of the screen and the whole of a store-listing screenshot. Placed next to reference/shots/ui-bar.png in an App Store listing, ours looks like the unfinished one at a glance.
